guarantees.claim: a1_inv[0] is continuously driven as s1 XOR mul_a0_b_inv_buf
a1_inv[1] is continuously driven as a1_inv_buf[0] XOR mul_a0_t_buf
a1_inv[2] is continuously driven as a1_inv_buf[1] XOR mul_m0_b_inv_buf
a1_inv[3] is continuously driven as a1_inv_buf[2] XOR mul_m0_t_buf
a0_inv[0] is continuously driven as s0 XOR mul_a1_b_inv_buf
a0_inv[1] is continuously driven as a0_inv_buf[0] XOR mul_a1_t_buf
a0_inv[2] is continuously driven as a0_inv_buf[1] XOR mul_m1_b_inv_buf
a0_inv[3] is continuously driven as a0_inv_buf[2] XOR mul_m1_t_buf

assumptions.claim: All input signals (s1, mul_a0_b_inv_buf, a1_inv_buf[0:2], mul_a0_t_buf, mul_m0_b_inv_buf, mul_m0_t_buf, s0, mul_a1_b_inv_buf, a0_inv_buf[0:2], mul_a1_t_buf, mul_m1_b_inv_buf, mul_m1_t_buf) must be valid (non-X) and stable during any sample of a1_inv or a0_inv.
assumptions.risk: X propagation can corrupt the masked inverse output, potentially breaking the AES S‑box calculation and leading to ciphertext errors or weakened fault resistance.

uncertain_points.claim: The combinational XOR assignments may produce glitches on a1_inv/a0_inv if any input is not registered or not stable within a clock phase, potentially leaking intermediate masked values through power traces.
uncertain_points.cond: when inputs change and the outputs are used before settling
uncertain_points.risk: First-order power side‑channel leakage of secret key material.

uncertain_points.claim: Correctness and first‑order masking security depend on s0 and s1 being independent random mask shares and on all mul_*_buf signals being correctly computed masked products; those properties must be verified in the driving logic.
uncertain_points.risk: If s0/s1 are not properly randomized or mul_*_buf are not masked, the output may be unmasked or leak statistical correlations.
